transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess... well, they brought me in because of what's been happening at work. I work at a warehouse, and... I keep doing things that bother people. Like, sometimes I just freeze with my arms up when I'm standing by the forklift. Or I'll start copying the beeping sounds the machines make, and doing the hand signals the drivers use. And when I'm supposed to be moving boxes, I end up putting them in these strange little patterns instead. People yell at me to stop and do it right, but... I just keep doing it. So they wanted me to come see you.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
No, I... I don't think so. I hear the actual machines and the people talking, but... nothing that isn't really there. Nobody's talking to me when I'm alone or anything like that.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory or your ability to think clearly lately?

I think... yeah, my thinking gets pretty messed up. It's hard to keep my thoughts straight when I talk. Like, when the supervisor asks me which pallets are going on the truck, I'll start trying to explain it to him. But my words just jump around. I'll start talking about the load sheet, and then somehow I'm talking about my old house, and then fishing... and then church boxes. 

I don't really know how I get from one thing to the next, but by the time I'm done talking, nobody knows what I meant. So, yeah, I guess I can't think clearly enough to just answer a simple question anymore.
Have you ever had any head injuries, seizures, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions that affect your brain or nervous system?

No, I... no. I've never had a seizure or hit my head really hard or anything like that. And I haven't been diagnosed with any kind of brain condition or nerve problems before. Physically, I'm... I'm fine, really. It's just all this other stuff happening.
Are these periods where you hold your arms up or copy the machine sounds something that happens for hours at a time, or do they happen in shorter bursts?

I'm not really sure what you mean. I don't hold my arms up in the air like that. And I definitely don't copy the sounds the machines make. I mean, I hear the forklifts and the belts running, but I'm not... I'm not making those noises myself. So, neither, I guess. That just doesn't happen to me.

I am a bit confused; earlier you mentioned that you were freezing with your arms up and copying sounds at work, but just now you said that does not happen to you—could you clarify if those things are actually happening, or if you were perhaps just imagining them?

Sorry, I... my head is just really mixed up today. No, it is actually happening. I guess that's the main reason they brought me in here. 

At the warehouse, I keep doing things like... freezing with my arms up by the forklift. And I do copy the beeping sounds and the hand signals. I'll also start moving boxes around in these strange little patterns, and I just keep doing it even when everyone is yelling for me to stop. 

So, yeah, I'm not imagining it. It really is happening, I just... I get confused and lose track of what I'm saying sometimes.
When you are performing these repetitive movements or copying the sounds, do you feel a strong emotional reaction like fear or joy, or do you feel emotionally empty and indifferent?

I don't really feel much of anything when I'm doing it. I'm not scared, and I'm definitely not happy about it. It's just... I just feel kind of blank, I guess. Empty. Like I'm just going through the motions and the feelings are turned off.
Are these periods of freezing and repeating movements happening every single day, or are there days where you are able to act and move completely normally?

I'm not really sure. It's hard to keep track of the days right now. I mean... I don't know if it's every single day, or if I have normal days in between where I don't do those things. It all just kind of blurs together in my head, honestly. So I can't really tell you for sure.
When you are at home or away from the warehouse, do you still find yourself freezing in place or repeating those same movements, or do these things only happen while you are at work?

I... I honestly don't know. I know it happens at the warehouse because my boss or the other guys yell at me about it. But when I'm at home... I'm really not sure. 

There's nobody there to point it out to me if I do freeze up or start doing those things. So I might be doing it in my apartment too, but I just haven't noticed, or I just don't remember. I really couldn't tell you.
How long have you been experiencing these periods of freezing or repeating movements—has this been going on for a few weeks, or has this been happening for months or even years?

I think... it's been about six months now. Yeah, around six months. That's when the guys at the warehouse started getting on me about the strange behavior, and... and my talking not making sense to them. So, it's been going on for about half a year.

When you are at the warehouse, are these physical behaviors—like freezing or copying the sounds—the main thing that others notice about you, or is your disorganized speech and confusion the primary problem that people complain about?

I think they complain about my talking the most, honestly. Like... when the supervisor asks me which pallets are going on the truck, I start trying to explain it to him. But my words just kind of jump around. 

I'll go from talking about the load sheet to... to my old house, and then fishing, and then church boxes. I don't really mean to, but by the time I'm done talking, nobody knows what I meant. So yeah, the confusion and the way I talk is a really big problem for them.

When you are having these episodes at work, do you feel that the freezing and copying of sounds are the most prominent and concerning behaviors, or does the confusion and jumbled speech happen more often and affect your day-to-day life more significantly than the physical movements?

I think... I mean, I kind of just answered that, but yeah, it's definitely the talking. The jumbled speech is what happens the most, and it's what messes up my day the most. 

The freezing and the copying sounds, I mean, it happens, but the talking is what really gets in the way. If I can't even tell them what pallets go where without getting confused, I can't really do my job right. So the confusion and the talking is the biggest issue, for sure.

When you are having these episodes, does the freezing and repeating of sounds occur as a reaction to your own jumbled thoughts, or do those physical behaviors happen completely independently of what you are thinking or saying at that moment?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't... I don't know if they're connected. Sometimes I'll just be standing there and my body just gets stuck, or I'll hear a sound and just make it back. I don't really notice what I'm thinking right when it happens. It just... happens.

Are there times when you are completely unable to move or speak for an extended period, or do you always maintain the ability to interact with others even when you are having these episodes of freezing and repeating movements?

I don't really interact with them when it happens. I guess that's actually why they brought me in to see you. 

At the warehouse, I keep doing things like... freezing with my arms up right by the forklift. Or I'll be copying the backup beeping sounds and the hand signals, or just moving boxes around in these strange little patterns. And even when everyone is yelling at me to stop, I just... I don't. I can't really snap out of it to answer them or stop what I'm doing. So I guess I do lose the ability to interact during those times.

When you are not experiencing these physical episodes, do you find that your behavior is generally silly, giggly, or lacking in goal-directed purpose, or do you feel that your personality and actions are typically quite serious and focused?

I don't really act silly or giggly, no. I mean, when I'm not getting stuck or confused, I'm just trying to do my job. I take it seriously. I just want to move the pallets and get through my shift. So, yeah, I'd say I'm pretty focused normally... I definitely wouldn't say I'm laughing around or acting goofy or anything like that.
When you are speaking with others, do you ever find yourself suddenly laughing or smiling when the situation is not actually funny or when you are talking about something serious?

No, I don't think so. I mean, if we're talking about something serious, I'm serious. I don't just start laughing for no reason. I don't really smile much at work anyway, to be honest. It's just... it's just a warehouse, you know? There's not really a lot to laugh about. So, no, I wouldn't say I do that.
